label: 01-artifact

label: 02-members
detail: Full member inventory: 4 TypeDefs, 2 Fields, 8 MethodDefs, 15 MemberRefs, call_edges, field_accesses, user_strings (empty -- no ldstr anywhere, no #US heap), per-method CIL anchors/opcode_counts/exception_regions.
Read REA artifact-inspection evidence record.
Pretty-printed 02-members.stdout.json to scratchpad (members_pretty.json) for paginated reading; not a deliverable, written outside reconstruction/pass05.
Read full member-inspection evidence in two chunks: types/fields/methods/anchors/opcode_counts, then member_refs/call_edges/field_accesses/user_strings/coverage/limitations.

Noted user_strings.literals is empty with no #US heap (metadata stream_names only #Blob/#GUID/#Strings/#~); combined with the task's hint about FieldRVA-backed data, hypothesized a runtime XOR-decode-from-embedded-byte-array string scheme keyed by method m_5558f5ab53(start,len,key) on type T84d29266f2.

Wrote a standalone ECMA-335 CIL decoder (standard 1-byte and 0xFE-prefixed 2-byte opcode tables) to resolve exact instruction sequences beyond REA's curated anchors, as explicitly permitted by the task brief.

First run used REA's reported file_offset as the first CIL byte directly; output did not match REA's own anchors (garbage opcodes), revealing file_offset actually points to the START of the tiny/fat method header, not past it.

Confirmed via raw byte inspection at file offsets 592 and 749 that the fat header fields (flags/maxstack/codesize/localvarsigtok) and the tiny header byte exactly reproduce REA's reported max_stack/il_size/local_var_sig_token/header_format, proving file_offset = header start. Corrected decoder to skip 1 byte (tiny) / 12 bytes (fat) before decoding CIL.

Re-ran corrected decoder; produced a full, self-consistent instruction listing for all 8 MethodDefs whose per-method instruction counts exactly match REA's reported instruction_count for every method (including Main's 172 instructions and exception region).
Parsed the PE section table and CLI header directly from PixelTone.exe bytes (DOS/NT headers, .text/.rsrc sections) to build an RVA-to-file-offset mapper.

Manually reconstructed the #~ metadata table layout (Module/TypeRef/TypeDef/Field/MethodDef/Param/MemberRef/CustomAttribute/ClassLayout/StandAloneSig/FieldRVA/Assembly/...) from ECMA-335 row-size formulas and cross-checked every computed row_offset against REA's reported row_offset values; all matched exactly, confirming 2-byte heap/table-index widths and the FieldRVA row's file location (offset 3438: 4-byte RVA + 2-byte Field index).
Read the FieldRVA entry (RVA 0x27c8 -> file offset 2504), extracted the 235-byte embedded blob referenced by field 0x04000001 / materialized into static field f_134b552a1f by .cctor.

Decoded all 11 distinct (start,length,key) call sites to T84d29266f2.m_5558f5ab53 against the recovered blob using the XOR-per-byte scheme read from the decoded CIL of m_5558f5ab53; every result was clean printable ASCII (help text, error messages, preset names, output format string), which is strong corroborating evidence the decode algorithm and blob extraction are both correct.

static_implementation_complete_utc anchor.

Verified mono/luma formula and negative-intermediate clamp boundary; result 0,0,0|4AB0F7B7 matched prediction.

Verified the inferred control-flow quirk: a single non-'--help' argument falls through to the generic 6-argument-count check rather than a distinct error path; exit 2 and message matched prediction exactly. Probe budget exhausted (8/8 used).
Ran pixel_tone.py against all 8 probe argument sets and diffed raw stdout/stderr bytes against the captured real-exe output.

Diff revealed probes 3, 4 and 5 crashed with ValueError: Invalid format specifier X8. The script had copied the C# composite-format spec {3:X8} verbatim into a Python str.format call, but Python needs width before type (08X), not X8. Fixed by building the output line with an explicit 08X spec.
Re-ran all 8 probes through the corrected pixel_tone.py; every stdout/stderr byte stream and exit code matched the real PixelTone.exe exactly (8/8).
Wrote the full probe audit log (command, exact stdout/stderr bytes, exit code, start/end timestamps, purpose, and confirmation note) for all 8 live invocations.
